memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work.** The deal passes every hard filter: asset type, freehold single title, area, unit count, price band, building age, Year-1 DSCR and no related-party master lease. It misses all three return tests: going-in yield, levered IRR and equity multiple.

**Recommendation:** don't go to full diligence at the asking price of AED 83.00m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. Re-engage only at or below AED 70.06m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], which is 15.59% [[uw.walk_away_discount_to_asking]] under asking. Levered IRR sets that price.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Cedarline Residences, Dubai Silicon Oasis. 112 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2013 [[deal.completion_year]], G+P+7.
- **Price:** AED 83.00m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], or AED 782 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]] on NSA, which is the OM's stated basis. Per sq ft of BUA it is AED 579 [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]].
- **Income:** in-place rent of AED 7.80m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] on direct leases with no master tenant. 106 units are let [[rr.let_units]] and 6 are vacant [[rr.vacant_units]], so occupancy is 94.64% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]]. Of the let units, 3 are under renewal [[rr.status.under_renewal]] and 2 have served notice [[rr.status.notice_served]]. The landlord pays chiller costs.

## Returns and key metrics
| Metric | Screen | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Year-1 NOI | AED 5.12m [[uw.noi_year1]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.81% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | at least 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] (fails) |
| Year-1 DSCR | 1.47x [[uw.dscr_year1]] | at least 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] (passes) |
| Levered IRR, pre-tax | 1.08% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] | at least 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] (fails) |
| Equity multiple, pre-tax | 1.05x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | at least 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]] (fails) |

The OM headline yield is 5.90% [[om.yield_stated]], net on total cost. On the OM's own income and basis I get 5.89% [[uw.om_yield.reproduced_on_om_basis]], so the headline reconciles. The buyer's basis is Year-1 NOI over price plus acquisition costs, which gives 5.81% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The headline is honest but still below the 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum. Total cost is AED 88.16m [[uw.total_cost_aed]].

## What would make it fail
- **Exit pricing.** The base exit yield is 7.00% [[uw.exit_yield]]. That gives a gross exit value of AED 78.49m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]], below the purchase price, and the levered exit result is a loss. With the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, levered IRR is -1.07% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]].
- **Market rent.** With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the base exit yield, levered IRR is -1.89% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. Even with market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, IRR is only 5.89% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.levered_irr_pre_tax]], still under the 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] target. No cell in the grid reaches the target. Debt cover holds in every case, with the weakest at 1.42x [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.dscr_year1]].
- **Rollover concentration.** The heaviest three-month window runs from 31 January 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] to 29 April 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. It holds AED 2.24m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]] of rent, or 28.7% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]], inside the 40.00% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]] limit. It is still a large block to renew in the first year.
- **Reversion upside is the OM's claim, not ours.** The OM says 21 tenancies [[om.upside_claim_1]] are let well below the rent index and can be raised at renewal. The screen's market rent reference is AED 9.21m [[uw.market_rent_reference_aed]], against in-place rent of AED 7.80m [[uw.in_place_rent_aed]]. The base case still assumes market rents fall 4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1. If the reversion is real, the base case is conservative. If it isn't, there is no cushion. About 9.90% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of income comes from units let above market reference, inside the 20.00% [[mandate.max_over_rent_share_of_income.threshold]] limit.

## Discrepancies that matter
The facts list no discrepancies between the documents. Every OM field verified, and none was missing. The rent roll ties to the OM on in-place rent, unit count and area. Occupancy is 94.64% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] on the rent roll against 94.60% [[om.occupancy_stated]] in the OM. The one gap worth noting is the yield gap above, which is small and explained by the basis. Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Before diligence, check
- Legal title and ownership confirmation.
- Lease-by-lease check of the rent roll, including expiry dates and the status of units under renewal or notice.
- Evidence for the OM's reversion claim, tested against the current RERA rent-increase bands and rental index.
- Support for the market rent reference and for the assumption that rents fall in Year 1.
- Twelve months of invoices and bank statements behind the operating statement, especially district cooling, which the landlord pays.
- Security deposit ledger and transfer mechanics.
- Lender term sheet confirming leverage, pricing and amortisation.
- Buyer-side acquisition cost quote.

## Assumptions
